messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Route /v1/stream (us-west-2) p99 breach. Recent metrics: p95=380ms, p99=4.1s, error-rate spike ~0.8%. Streaming stalls and long tail observed. source=gw-37a, impacted pool=gpu-pool-3

sasha: I'm oncall for US right now, taking lead. tagging @devon for infra checks and @amber for customer impact.

devon: pulling node telemetry now. gw-37a shows GPU fan ramp and rising junction temp. ECC correctable errors increasing on accel-37. Running `nvidia-smi -q -d TEMPERATURE,FAULT`

leo: grabbing logs from runtime, see repeated `KV cache stall` entries around token 1024 for a subset of requests. Could be page-in / ECC recovery pauses.

sasha: amber — which customers hit the SLO? need to know severity for paging.

amber: Support summary: two high-throughput customers saw degraded streaming responsiveness — session ids: `sess-8f3a`, `sess-d2b1`. No full request failures, just stalls (clients reconnecting). Raising priority P1 for revenue-impacting tenants.

jordan: Noted. Routing: auto-fallback triggered to smaller-quantized variant for ~20% of traffic but that has different latency profile. Might be exacerbating tail.

devon: here's quick health snapshot (excerpt):
```
Node: gw-37a
GPU: accel-37
Temp (junction): 105C -> 110C over 8m
ECC corr errors: 112 -> 340
Fan RPM: 4200 -> 5200
Throttle state: thermal_running
Kernel messages: ECC recovery interrupts every ~15s
```

devon: I’m going to cordon gw-37a and bounce the worker to force routing off it. Will drain in-flight requests gracefully (streaming will fallback).

sasha: Do it. Set `drain_mode=graceful` and route traffic to gpu-pool-4. Also, enable short-term canary of model variant that avoids KV-heavy ops (reduce prefix caching) to see effect.

devon: commands executed:
```
# mark node unschedulable
redwoodctl nodes cordon gw-37a --reason "thermal-ecc-p99-spike"
# drain
redwoodctl nodes drain gw-37a --grace-period 30s
```

incidents-bot: ACTION: Node gw-37a cordoned and draining. Estimated failover completion ~45s.

leo: After routing shift, p99 dropped to ~1.2s for most routes. A small subset still hitting 2.4s due to in-flight KV stalls. Monitoring tail.

sasha: Amber — please prepare customer comms: impacted sessions had stalliness but resumed. Recommend note: short-term degraded latency, mitigation in progress, root-cause investigation ongoing.

amber: Drafting comms now. Will include affected session ids and advise customers to retry streaming session if they saw reconnects.

jordan: Post-mortem checklist: collect ECC logs, GPU microcode version, kernel oops, and any recent driver updates. Also correlate with last maintenance window (was there a microcode push?).

devon: Found last driver push to gw-37* on 5276540000 (yesterday) — version mismatch on one rack? Pulling deployment diff.

leo: Also seeing increased GC on runtime around the same window — could be combined pressure (thermal + software path).

sasha: Current action items: 1) node remains drained and out of rotation; 2) escalate hardware team to inspect accel-37 for potential flaky ECC; 3) place automation to avoid auto-routing to nodes with >100 ECC corr errors for 30m; 4) follow-up postmortem.

devon: Created incident ticket INF-2026-5276 and assigned to infra/hardware. I've added logs and the `nvidia-smi` output.

amber: Customer comms sent to affected accounts: AcmeCo and Finlytics (internal ref #INC-5276). They acknowledged, want ETA on root cause.

incidents-bot: UPDATE: p99 back to ~600ms cluster-wide after drain and fallback. Still watching for recurring ECC flares.

jordan: Next steps: schedule hardware swap if ECC persists after inspection, otherwise put GPU into quarantine and replace node. Also run extended soak tests on replacement.

leo: saving diagnostic bundle: `s3://redwood-diagnostics/5276543210-gpu-thermal-hiccup.tgz` (logs, metrics, stack traces).

sasha: Thanks team. I'm un-assigning myself once infra confirms hardware triage. Keep this thread for follow-ups only. If anything spikes again, re-paging. :thumbsup:

amber: closing the paging loop with customers; will coordinate postmortem timeline.

devon: infra taking over for hardware poke. Leaving node in quarantine flag.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigating -> monitoring.

sasha: last note — add alert rule to trigger earlier on ECC corr error rate slope (not just absolute count). We nearly missed the ramp.

leo: filed alert PR: #3421, sets slope trigger over 2m window.

support-bot: Logged customer impact and comms in ticketing system: RB-98321.

sasha: thanks all. ending thread.
